observedAgainst: main plus the active uncommitted working tree

currentBatch.title: Market map credibility baseline
currentBatch.objective: Remove undefined authority signals and false taxonomy structure from the public market map.
constraints: Do not change route slugs, primary navigation, the locked wordmark, the engineering grid, typography, palette, or social cards.
Do not edit data/companies.ts by hand. Change the research source of truth and regenerate when company data must change.
Preserve every source link, as-of date, unknown value, keyboard path, and working deep link unless an acceptance criterion explicitly changes it.
Do not add a replacement score, progress meter, card treatment, marketing copy, feature, or general refactor.
Do not begin backlog findings outside this batch.
requiredHandoff: Unresolved decisions and known collateral changes
stopConditions: A required change would alter the six top-level market segments or the /market-map/ route.
A rewrite would require a factual claim that is not supported by an existing source.
Another writer is editing the same files.
The batch cannot preserve existing source links or honest unknown values.

findings.title: Public confidence badges imply a methodology the product does not expose
evidence: The public route labels 47 companies high confidence, 48 medium, and 16 low.
The source schema records only URL, title, and as-of date. It does not encode source class, claim coverage, verification method, or a reason for the row-level confidence label.
The UI turns the three labels into green, amber, and red badges and offers Confidence as a filter without explaining what is being scored.
acceptanceCriteria: Remove the public Confidence filter and high, medium, and low badges from /market-map/ for this release.
Keep the internal confidence field unchanged so this batch does not trigger an unsupported 111-row data migration.
Drop legacy confidence query parameters safely while preserving all valid sibling filters.
Keep company source links and as-of dates visible.
State once, in plain language, that source links and dates are shown per company and unknown figures remain not disclosed.
Update focused component, unit, and deep-link tests to match the public behaviour.
mustNot: Do not replace confidence with another score, stars, verification percentage, traffic light, or vague provenance badge.
Do not recolour the badges and call the problem fixed.
Do not remove or weaken source links, as-of dates, or honest unknown values.

findings.title: The approach filter exposes generated descriptors as if they were a usable taxonomy
evidence: 111 companies contain 238 approach assignments and 191 unique approach values.
168 of the 191 approach values occur on exactly one company.
lib/market-map.ts creates the public filter directly from every raw approach value, so the control is a list of descriptors rather than a navigable classification.
acceptanceCriteria: Expose no more than 30 reviewed categories in the public Approach filter.
Every public filter category maps to at least two companies.
Preserve useful company-specific approach descriptors as row metadata without automatically promoting each descriptor into a filter option.
Keep valid existing deep links working where the old value has a clear canonical category; safely drop values that have no honest mapping.
Add a focused deterministic test that reports company count, assignment count, public category count, and singleton public category count.
The public category singleton count must be zero.
mustNot: Do not solve this by hiding the select while leaving the same public taxonomy elsewhere.
Do not merge technically distinct concepts solely to hit the count.
Do not invent company capabilities or rewrite sourced facts.

findings.title: Company descriptions read like one generated template
evidence: 78 of 111 company descriptions begin with the word Builds.
The repetition makes independently sourced records sound batch-generated even when the facts are sound.
acceptanceCriteria: No single opening word is used by more than 25 percent of company descriptions.
Each edited description remains one concise factual sentence.
Every factual change is supported by an existing row source; unsupported variation is prohibited.
Add a corpus-level repetition test that prints the dominant opening and its share.
mustNot: Do not use a thesaurus to rotate Builds into Develops, Creates, and Makes while preserving the same sentence template.
Do not add slogans, adjectives, valuations, or deployment claims for variety.

findings.title: The homepage makes an absolute citation claim that current validation cannot prove
evidence: The homepage says every claim is cited to a primary source.

Current validation resolves citation IDs, registry metadata, links, references, and selected route-specific claims, but it does not classify every sentence-level claim or prove that every source is primary.
acceptanceCriteria: Either narrow the public claim to the policy the repository actually enforces, or add a claim-level audit that can substantiate the absolute wording.
Distinguish primary, first-party, independent secondary, aggregator, and snippet-grade evidence where those classes affect public certainty.
The final wording must remain concrete and must not imply universal verification from citation presence alone.
mustNot: Do not add another trust slogan or verification percentage.
Do not treat a resolving URL as proof that the linked source supports the surrounding claim.

findings.title: Article cross-reference prose repeats the same generated frame
evidence: 27 of 47 MDX articles contain the exact phrase at the top of this module.
The phrase is structural filler and often describes layout position instead of the mechanism being taught.
acceptanceCriteria: No stock cross-reference phrase appears in more than 20 percent of articles.
Edited sentences name the specific diagram, timeline, table, or interaction and state what it demonstrates.
Rewrites preserve the technical claim and existing citations.
Add a corpus-level exact-phrase and repeated-n-gram report.
mustNot: Do not rotate among near-synonyms such as figure above, chart above, and graphic above solely to pass a string test.
Do not move figures or rewrite technical conclusions in this batch.

findings.title: Some article copy names green marks after the shared interaction colour moved to signal blue
evidence: The generalist-policies article says green nodes are downloadable while the current component and chart description use signal blue for open weights.
The JEPA article calls the current latent marker green while the interaction now uses the accent token for active state.
acceptanceCriteria: Every visible legend, article sentence, accessible description, and rendered mark agrees on the semantic state and colour.
Prefer state names such as open weights or current latent over colour names when colour is not the concept.
Run the locked VAL-BRAND-008 and chart-description checks across every interactive route, not only the two examples.
mustNot: Do not restore green merely to preserve stale prose if the mark represents selection rather than success.
Do not fix visible text while leaving ARIA or ChartDescription copy stale.
